data_shape: continuous value over ordered time/sequence
discrete categories with one numeric measure each
best_for: comparing values across a handful of categories

data_shape: discrete categories, especially with long labels
best_for: ranked lists with long category names

data_shape: categories with multiple sub-series summing to a total
avoid_for: comparing individual sub-series precisely across bars — stacking makes that hard to read

data_shape: multiple time series summing to a meaningful total
single part-to-whole breakdown, few categories
best_for: 2-5 category composition where the 'whole' matters visually
avoid_for: comparing two different pies side by side

data_shape: single part-to-whole breakdown with a central summary metric
best_for: composition plus a headline total/percentage in the center

data_shape: two continuous numeric variables per point, optionally a third via size/color
two categorical axes with one numeric intensity value per cell
avoid_for: fewer than ~9 cells (a table is clearer)

data_shape: single compressed trend, no axes/labels
best_for: inline trend context next to a KPI number

data_shape: sequential stages with decreasing counts
best_for: conversion/drop-off across a fixed sequence of steps

data_shape: single value against a fixed min/max range or target
OHLC (open/high/low/close) per time period
avoid_for: general audiences unfamiliar with the convention

data_shape: hierarchical part-to-whole with size as the numeric measure
best_for: nested composition (e.g. spend by category then subcategory)
many categories where a pie would fail

data_shape: multiple metrics on comparable normalized scales for one or few entities
best_for: multi-attribute comparison (e.g. skill ratings, feature scores) for 1-3 entities

data_shape: single continuous numeric variable binned into ranges
best_for: distribution shape of a single metric across a population

data_shape: distribution summary (median, quartiles, outliers) per category
best_for: comparing distributions across categories, especially for technical/analytical audiences
avoid_for: general consumer audiences unfamiliar with the convention

data_shape: actual value vs. target vs. qualitative ranges, one per row
best_for: dense dashboard rows comparing actual-vs-target across many metrics at once

data_shape: numeric value per geographic region
avoid_for: precise value comparison between distant regions

data_shape: sequential positive/negative deltas building to a running total
best_for: explaining how a starting value moves to an ending value (e.g. revenue bridge)

data_shape: one numeric value per calendar day over a year
avoid_for: precise value comparison across distant dates
